item.title: [8] Borrowed Planckian dissipation in magic-angle twisted graphene
item.description:
Last authors: Dino \v{S}krgi\'c, Dejan Stojkovic

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental-focused study on transport in twisted bilayer graphene systems, relevant to broader moire interests.

Tags: #transport #graphene #moire

Abstract: In strange metals, the ratio of the coefficients producing signature linear-in-$T$ resistivity and the logarithmic specific heat is free of the coupling between the electrons and whatever scatters them. In the materials studied so far that coupling is fixed by chemistry. Magic-angle twisted trilayer graphene provides a dial with a displacement field $D$ that breaks the mirror symmetry separating a light Dirac cone from the flat bands, and the Dirac carriers borrow the Planckian self-energy of the flat band with a weight proportional to $D^2+D_0^2$. Resistance curves taken at eight fields are consistent with the field acting on the scattering rate rather than on the number of carriers. The slope in temperature follows $a(1+D^2/D_0^2)$ without the quartic term that a depleting Dirac pocket adds, and the elastic part varies by less than 5\% between 0.20 and 0.30~V/nm while the inelastic part grows 2.5-fold up to 0.38~V/nm. The thermally averaged Kubo formula favors flat-band weight placed symmetrically about the Fermi level over a single level. Borrowed dissipation keeps the bath exponent and transport prefactor of the flat band's own electrons but carries exactly twice their entropy per unit of borrowed coupling whenever the bath has dynamics of its own, so the field-differential ratio is $2\pi^3/21\zeta(3)\approx2.46$ for a conformal flat band and, in a numerical search, at most 2.73 for monotonic bath spectra without a high-energy rate floor. The discriminating test is the entropy measured in steps of $D$.

item.title: [7] Neutron Scattering studies of the density dependence of One-dimensional Quantum Fluids
item.description:
Last authors: Adrian Del Maestro, Paul E. Sokol

Authors: Sutirtha Paul, Rahul Soni, Garfield Warren, Adrian Del Maestro, Paul E. Sokol

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study using neutron scattering on 1D quantum fluids, relevant to broader condensed matter interests.

Tags: #neutronscattering #1Dmaterials #fluids

Abstract: In previous work, we demonstrated that $^4$He confined within a templated porous material preplated with a noble gas to enhance dimensional reduction exhibits one-dimensional behavior. Neutron scattering revealed that the excitations in confined $^4$He are qualitatively distinct from those in two- and three-dimensional superfluid helium, aligning with quantum Monte Carlo calculations. These simulations suggest that three solid layers form, with a one-dimensional liquid located at the center of the pore. Here, we present neutron scattering results as the filling fraction of the one-dimensional core is varied. We observe that the one-dimensional liquid always forms with a fixed density, even as the pore filling increases. We posit that this is due to the growth of the one dimensional extent of the liquid as the filling is increased, but its density remains unchanged.

item.title: [8] Hybridization-brightened interlayer excitons in multilayer WSe2 controlled by sliding ferroelectricity
item.description:
Last authors: Jing-Yang You, Moshe Ben Shalom

Authors: Youngki Yeo, Idan Kizel, Dror Hershkovitz, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study on 2D materials (WSe2) and ferroelectricity, within the user's scope of van der Waals materials.

Tags: #WSe2 #ferroelectricity #excitons

Abstract: Interlayer excitons (IXs) combine spatially separated electron and hole wavefunctions with electrically tunable dipole moments, but their reduced wavefunction overlap generally limits optical emission, particularly for high-energy states. Here we report a bright, spectrally narrow high-energy interlayer exciton (h-IX) near 2.23 eV in few-layer WSe2 and investigate how its optical activity evolves with layer number and sliding-ferroelectric polarization. In pristine 2H-WSe2, we observe thickness-dependent brightening of high-energy exciton emission. GW-BSE calculations reveal mixed intralayer and interlayer configurations with enhanced optical weight, suggesting that multilayer hybridization contributes to the observed brightening. In parallel-stacked 3L/3L WSe2 containing a sliding-ferroelectric interface, the h-IX exhibits polarization-dependent energies and Stark responses that distinguish Pup and Pdown domains. Electric-field-driven domain-wall motion produces hysteretic transfer of spectral weight between the two h-IX branches, enabling optical tracking of ferroelectric switching. These results establish multilayer hybridization as a route to optically active high-energy interlayer excitons and sliding ferroelectricity as a complementary degree of freedom for controlling their energy, dipole and emission.

item.title: [9] A Perspective on Topological Charge Density Wave Materials
item.description:
Last authors: Alexander A. Balandin, Md Shafayat Hossain

Authors: Chun-Tung Lien, Nidhish Thiruthukkal Puthenveettil, Alexander A. Balandin, Md Shafayat Hossain

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Directly addresses topological CDW, kagome, and electronic structure order relevant to AV3Sb5 materials.

Tags: #material #topic

Abstract: Charge density waves are among the earliest known ordered states in quantum materials, yet they have re-emerged at the center of modern discussions of topology, symmetry breaking, and collective dynamics. In several material classes, charge-density-wave order reshapes electronic bands, boundary states, defect structures, and electromagnetic responses in ways that invite a topological interpretation. Real-space imaging has shown that incommensurate order can form networks of phase defects rather than uniform modulations. Boundary-resolved spectroscopy has revealed in-gap modes whose existence and spatial structure track the charge-density-wave order, although such observations remain confined to a single material family. In Weyl materials, density-wave gaps have been linked to axion-like magnetoelectric response, placing the charge-density-wave phase within a dynamical-field description of the effective action. In kagome metals, charge order is intertwined with Berry curvature, unconventional symmetry breaking, and superconductivity. These developments have led to the term "topological charge density wave," but the phrase describes several physically distinct phenomena. We distinguish three meanings: (i) topology of the order parameter and its defects, (ii) topology of the charge-density-wave-reconstructed electronic structure and its boundary modes, and (iii) axion-like electromagnetic response generated by density-wave order. The experimental and theoretical support for these three meanings differs substantially. This Perspective traces the development of these ideas, clarifies the evidence behind each class, identifies unresolved questions and points of debate, and outlines experimental criteria for establishing topology in charge-density-wave states.

item.title: [7] Geometry-Selective Higher-order topological insulators induced by dxy altermagnet
item.description:
Last authors: Xiaosen Yang, Yuanping Chen

Authors: Siyuan Cheng, Yuee Xie, Xiaosen Yang, Yuanping Chen

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Topical altermagnetism research with implications for electronic structure and topological phases.

Tags: #material #topic

Abstract: We show that proximity to a $d_{xy}$-wave altermagnet provides an effective route to engineering boundary-geometry-dependent higher-order topological phases. The boundary geometry plays a crucial role in determining the topological properties: axis-aligned edge states remain gapless, whereas diagonal edges acquire effective masses with alternating signs, giving rise to four corner modes localized at the mass domain walls. By projecting onto the edge-state subspace, we derive the effective edge Hamiltonians for different boundary geometries. Furthermore, $\pi$-flux defects introduced under periodic boundary conditions yield zero-energy bound states localized at the flux cores, providing complementary evidence for nontrivial topology without physical boundaries. The interplay between the Zeeman field and the altermagnetic order drives a topological transition through the closing and reopening of the edge gap, while the bulk gap remains open. These findings highlight the crucial role of boundary geometry in higher-order topology and establish proximity-induced $d_{xy}$-wave altermagnetism as a route to engineering higher-order topological phases.

item.title: [8] Magnetization-free quantum anomalous Hall effect in altermagnetic weak topological insulators (Phys. Rev. B)
item.description:
Last authors: Rundong Zhao, Qing-Feng Sun

Authors: Yanmiao Han, Yu-Hao Wan, Peng-Yi Liu, Rundong Zhao, Qing-Feng Sun

Published as: Phys. Rev. B DOI

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Combines altermagnetism with topological insulators, directly relevant to electronic band structure studies.

Tags: #material #topic

Abstract: The quantum anomalous Hall (QAH) effect is usually realized through ferromagnetism or magnetic dop ing, which limits material choices and often results in low mobility, disorder sensitivity, and low operating temperatures. Here, we propose a mechanism to achieve the QAH phase without net magnetization, using altermagnetic exchange on a weak topological insulator (WTI). The altermagnetic order selectively gaps the Dirac cone at the Z point, while hybridization between the top and bottom surfaces of the WTI thin film opens a trivial gap at the point, generating a Chern number C = 1 phase with a single chiral edge channel. We verify the topological transition through both a minimal thin-film model and a slab geometry, and compute the associated Hall response. As altermagnets and layered WTIs already exist experimentally, this mechanism offers a promising and experimentally accessible route to realizing QAH phases without magnetic doping or global magnetization. The results indicate that altermagnetic surface engineering may provide a clean and controllable pathway for realizing dissipationless edge transport in layered quantum materials.

item.title: [7] Field-induced magnetic quantum phase transitions in a bilayer triangular lattice antiferromagnet K2Co2(HPO3)2(C2O4)(H2O)2
item.description:
Last authors: Yi Cui, Hongcheng Lu

Authors: Yiqiu Liu, Chengcheng Yin, Xinyu Shi, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Strong experimental NMR study on frustrated magnetism, relevant to broader correlated electron systems.

Tags: #material #topic

Abstract: We present a $^{31}$P nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) study on the spin-$1/2$ bilayer triangular-lattice antiferromagnet K$_2$Co$_2$(HPO$_3$)$_2$(C$_2$O$_4$)(H$_2$O)$_2$. Measurements were performed at temperatures down to 0.06 K and magnetic fields up to 26 T. In the field range of 0.5 T to 4 T, the low-temperature spin-lattice relaxation rate $1/T_1$ exhibits a peak, signaling the onset of a magnetically ordered state. Within this ordered phase, $1/T_1$ shows gapless behavior, suggesting a spin supersolid phase. This ordering is suppressed around 4 T. Between 6 T and 18 T, clear splittings of the NMR spectra are observed, indicating the emergence of a second ordered magnetic phase. The field derivative of the low-temperature Knight shift $K_{\rm n}$ reveals changes in slope at approximately 10 T, 15.5 T, and 18 T. The first two features correspond to bulk magnetizations of $1/3$ and $2/3$ of the fully saturated moment, respectively, while the last one marks a quantum phase transition from the second ordered phase to the fully polarized state. These results establish the studied compound as a platform for investigating field-induced quantum phase transitions and emergent phases in frustrated bilayer triangular-lattice antiferromagnets.

item.title: [8] Hidden interfacial magnetism in RuO2 heterostructures revealed by a superconducting spin switch
item.description:
Last authors: F. Sebastian Bergeret, Teruo Ono

Authors: Tetsuma Mandokoro, Hisakazu Matsuki, Shutaro Karube, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Addresses altermagnetism/RuO2 interfacial physics using superconducting probes, highly relevant to electronic properties.

Tags: #material #topic

Abstract: RuO$_2$, once the flagship altermagnetic candidate, is now believed to be nonmagnetic in the bulk, yet weak, static and spatially inhomogeneous magnetism emerges at its surfaces and interfaces. Where this magnetism resides, what stabilises it, and whether it is connected to these states remain open questions. Here we address these questions at the Nb/RuO$_2$ interface using a superconducting spin switch. A GdN/Nb/RuO$_2$ trilayer allows interfacial exchange-field alignment to tune the superconducting transition temperature of Nb, probing interfacial magnetism inaccessible to conventional magnetometry. The switch reveals a hidden magnetic subsystem, which we attribute to a thin RuO$_x$ redox layer formed as Nb scavenges oxygen from RuO$_2$. This layer behaves as a weak and magnetically hard ferromagnet with vacancy-induced anisotropy. Furthermore, supercurrent amplifies the switching efficiency, making the probe sensitivity tunable in situ. Superconducting spin switches thus emerge as a quantitative low-temperature probe of hidden magnetism at buried interfaces.

item.title: [7] Chiral magnon Kerr interaction from linear and nonlinear Meissner screening in ferromagnet--superconductor bilayers
item.description:
Last authors: Hanchen Wang, Tao Yu

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant study on ferromagnet-superconductor heterostructures with potential experimental relevance.

Tags: #magnon #superconductor #heterostructure

Abstract: Magnon Kerr interaction showing a dependence of magnon dispersion frequency on its population is a useful functionality for nonlinear and quantum magnonics; its strength and sign depend on magnetic anisotropy, bias, and mode geometry. We here propose to use a superconducting gate to tune the Kerr interaction of magnons in ferromagnetic insulators. Even when the superconductor responds linearly, the frequency shift induced by its reflected dipolar field depends on the longitudinal magnetization. The decrease of this magnetization with increasing precession amplitude therefore produces a Kerr contribution. We go beyond this linear Meissner-screening regime by showing that at finite excitation amplitude, the significant Meissner screening currents reduce the superfluid stiffness, thus enhancing the effective magnetic-field penetration and rendering the Meissner backaction amplitude dependent. This superflow-induced pair breaking adds a second Kerr contribution, controlled by the interfacial superflow relative to the nonlinear screening scale. For yttrium iron garnet gated by dirty niobium, we predict a significant renormalization of the Kerr effect by superconductors, with the resulting Kerr contribution strongly chiral in the Damon--Eshbach configuration. By showing that the linear and nonlinear Meissner screening to the Kerr interaction can be distinguished by varying temperature, our work establishes a route to directional control of magnon nonlinear interactions.

item.title: [8] Evidence of anomalous Hall crystals in moir\'e rhombohedral graphene
item.description:
Last authors: Jie Shan, Kin Fai Mak

Authors: Hongyuan Li, Zuhan Geng, Annika Weber, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental evidence for anomalous Hall crystals in moiré graphene, relevant to Berry curvature.

Tags: #experiment #graphene #moire #anomalousHall #Berrycurvature #transport #Chern

Abstract: An anomalous Hall crystal (AHC) is a quantum state of matter, in which spontaneous electron crystallization leads to a quantized Hall effect without a magnetic field. The state can emerge in materials with strong Coulomb interaction and large Berry curvatures, such as few-layer rhombohedral graphene. Although the idea of AHCs has been invoked to explain some of the observed Chern insulators in moir\'e rhombohedral graphene (mRG), direct experimental evidence of AHCs has been missing so far. Here, we report experimental evidence of AHCs in hole-doped mRG through combined electrical transport and noise measurements. We identify a series of distinct Chern insulators spanning a broad and continuous range of doping densities incommensurate with the underlying moir\'e lattice; the states exhibit current-induced broadband noise and memory effects as well as pronounced gate hysteresis. Systematic magnetic field, temperature and gate dependence studies further support the emergence of a spontaneously charge-ordered state that acts as a parental state for the observed Chern insulators. The absence of Chern insulators at nearby integer fillings also distinguishes the observed state from the reported reentrant or extended quantum (anomalous) Hall states. Altogether, our results establish experimental evidence of AHCs in mRG and open the door for further exploration of the collective dynamics in this new state of matter.

Abstract: Whether a lightly doped Mott insulator on the square lattice supports robust $d$-wave superconductivity remains a central question in strongly correlated physics and in the microscopic theory of cuprate superconductivity. Abstract: Recent spin-sensitive scanning tunneling experiments with topological-insulator tips motivate a microscopic understanding of how tip geometry controls current delivery. Abstract: Several unconventional superconducting phases have been discovered in the vicinity of metamagnetism in the heavy-fermion paramagnet UTe$_2$ under magnetic field. item.title: [7] Edge quantum weight of finite Chern flakes and its topological floor
item.description:
Last authors: Rohit Narula

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory on topological Chern flakes, chiral edge modes, and circular dichroism, relevant to user's interests.

Tags: #theory #topological #Cherninsulator #edgestates #circulardichroism

Abstract: The zero-point energy of a circuit measures the polarization fluctuation of an insulator coupled to it. In a crystal this is the bulk quantum weight $K_\mathrm{bulk}$, which the Chern number $C$ bounds below by $|C|$. We show that a finite Chern flake adds an edge term that survives as the flake grows. The low-frequency transitions of its chiral edge carry a dipole weight, the sum of their squared dipole matrix elements, $K_\mathrm{edge}\geq|C|$ per unit area, a floor that follows from the positive absorption of both circular polarizations by every transition and the known cancellation of circular dichroism between edge and bulk. A weakly coupled circuit slower than the edge modes therefore reads $K_\mathrm{bulk}+K_\mathrm{edge}$, averaged over two field directions, while a faster one below the bulk gap approaches $K_\mathrm{bulk}$, so which quantum weight is measured depends on whether the flake is made large or the circuit slow first. Exact free-fermion calculations on lattice flakes bear out the floor and this dependence on the circuit frequency. The result holds at weak coupling, which a growing flake at fixed coupling eventually leaves. Above the floor, the edge weight of one channel is a number fixed by the shape of the boundary and the edge velocities, which square and rectangular lattice flakes follow to within 0.003. Each further edge channel adds its own such number, while the circular dichroism of the edge counts only the net chirality.

Abstract: We report a comprehensive investigation of the magnetic properties and spin dynamics of the chain-like van der Waals antiferromagnet AgCrP$_2$S$_6$ using magnetization, magnetic susceptibility, and $^{31}$P nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR). A constrained AF-FM zig-zag-chain calculation is also compatible with the susceptibility, supporting a dominant quasi one dimensional antiferromagnetic exchange scale of order 100 K. $^{31}$P NMR measurements provide microscopic insight into both static and dynamic spin correlations. The $K-\chi$ relation displays two distinct linear regimes separated near $T^\ast\approx 250$ K, with different slopes indicating a change in the effective transferred hyperfine couplings. Below $T_{N}$, the relaxation follows $1/T_1\propto T^5$, consistent with magnon-mediated relaxation in the ordered state. The temperature dependence of the internal hyperfine field yields a critical exponent $\beta\approx 0.36$, consistent with three-dimensional universality. Together, these results establish AgCrP$_2$S$_6$ as a quasi-one-dimensional $S=3/2$ antiferromagnet embedded in a layered van der Waals host, in which local probes directly resolve the crossover from correlated intrachain spin dynamics to anisotropic three-dimensional magnetic order. Abstract: We investigate the zero-temperature transition from the polarized normal phase to the FFLO state in a two-dimensional Fermi gas by means of a diagrammatic t-matrix approach. We first show that the standard non-self-consistent theory produces an unphysical critical polarization because of a severe violation of the Luttinger theorem. Motivated by this observation, we introduce a minimal self-consistent extension that largely restores compliance with the Luttinger theorem while preserving the analytical simplicity of the original formalism. Finally, for a three-dimensional lattice, we demonstrate within the Hertz-Millis framework that vertex corrections are irrelevant, thereby placing the FFLO quantum phase transition in the mean-field universality class, in close analogy with the itinerant antiferromagnet transition.

Last authors: S. Hughes

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Topical study on driven polaritons and gauge invariance, relevant for ARPES-related cavity materials.

Tags: #theory #floquet #polaritons

Abstract: Ultrastrong light--matter coupling of linear systems, such as Landau polaritons formed by a two-dimensional electron gas in a terahertz cavity, is described by the bosonic Hopfield model, and gauge invariance forbids a superradiant phase transition (SRPT). Modulating the magnetic field alone has been predicted to enhance the cycle-averaged coupling and induce a Floquet SRPT. We develop an exact theory of periodically driven Landau polaritons. Including the electric field induced by the modulated flux (Faraday's law), the problem reduces exactly, by Kohn's theorem, to the electronic center-of-mass mode coupled to the cavity, whose Hamiltonian is a sum of squares at every instant. A theorem of Krein then guarantees stability to all orders above a computable drive frequency, the Krein frequency, for which we give a self-contained proof. Below it, the system is stable except within resonance tongues where the drive creates pairs from the vacuum, the dynamical Casimir effect. At high drive frequency the electrons experience the mean field plus a ponderomotive trap (the Fock--Darwin problem), not an enhanced coupling. A gauge theorem excludes a Floquet photon condensate for any band structure, including Kane nonparabolicity, for which we derive a generalized Thomas--Reiche--Kuhn (TRK) sum rule. The predicted transition arises from averaging the coupling in a fixed Landau-level basis, which yields an effective model that violates the TRK sum rule; under driving, gauge invariance also requires the induced Faraday field. The rule to modulate and average the minimal-coupling Hamiltonian, not the parameters of its projection, applies to any linear, minimally coupled system. Instead of an SRPT, magnetic modulation produces dynamical Casimir emission: Faraday-driven polariton--magnetoplasmon pairs at low threshold, and two-color photon pairs with up to 5--10~dB of two-mode squeezing.

item.title: [8] Real-Space Visualization of Site-Selective Co 3d States in the Ising Magnet Ca3Co2O6 (J. Phys. Soc. Jpn.)
item.description:
Last authors: Yuichi Yamasaki, Taka-hisa Arima

Authors: Kamini Gautam, Shunsuke Kitou, Yuiga Nakamura, et al.

Published as: J. Phys. Soc. Jpn. DOI

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Excellent experimental spectroscopic visualization of orbital states in a quantum magnetic material.

Tags: #experiment #electronic-structure #magnetism

Abstract: High-spin Co3+ ions can retain a finite orbital contribution and exhibit pronounced magnetic anisotropy, providing model systems for Ising magnetism. However, direct real-space observations of their orbital states remain limited. Here, we visualize the site-dependent Co 3d electronic states in the Ising-chain magnet Ca3Co2O6, which contains crystallographically inequivalent high-spin and low-spin Co3+ sites, using synchrotron X-ray diffraction and valence electron density (VED) analysis based on core differential Fourier synthesis. The octahedral Co site exhibits a VED distribution consistent with a low-spin state, whereas the trigonal-prismatic Co site shows pronounced anisotropy that cannot be reproduced by crystal electric field (CEF) effects alone. A wavefunction analysis incorporating CEF effects, spin-orbit coupling, and ligand-mediated Co 3d-O 2p-Co 4p hybridization reproduces the observed VED anisotropy. These results establish a site-selective real-space picture of the Co electronic states and demonstrate the capability of VED analysis to probe local orbital states and orbital hybridization in quantum materials.

item.title: [7] Spontaneous breaking of a continuous symmetry at a non-conformal quantum critical point in one dimension (Phys. Rev. Research)
item.description:
Last authors: R. Flores-Calder\'on, M. Z\"undel

Published as: Phys. Rev. Research DOI

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant 1D quantum criticality study; useful for understanding spin-chain materials.

Tags: #theory #quantum-criticality #spin-chains

Abstract: In this work, we present numerical evidence for the spontaneous breaking of a continuous $U(1)$ symmetry in a nearest-neighbor interacting spin-1 chain at a quantum critical point separating two XY quasi-long-range ordered phases distinguished by a spontaneously broken $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry. Remarkably, the continuous symmetry breaking emerges precisely at the critical point of the discrete order parameter, suggesting a novel mechanism beyond currently established scenarios. At criticality, the XY correlations develop true long-range order, accompanied by a finite perpendicular magnetization, a zero-frequency Bragg peak in the transverse dynamical structure factor, and sharp gapless collective excitations. From complementary static and dynamical observables, we quantitatively determine the critical exponents, obtaining a dynamical exponent $z=1.50\pm0.04$ and an anomalous dimension $\eta=1.04\pm0.03$. We further show that the non-interacting continuum limit is equivalent to the recently introduced transverse quantum fluid, displaying their off-diagonal long-ranged order in one dimension. Complementing the numerical study, we derive the renormalization-group flow equations of the continuum theory to second order in the $\varepsilon$ expansion. We identify an interacting fixed point whose critical behavior differs from the Ising universality class already at two-loop order, although the perturbative exponents remain far from the numerical values.

item.title: [7] Interfacial charge-transfer in 3d/5d complex oxide heterostructures
item.description:
Last authors: Matthieu Le Tacon, Dirk Fuchs

Authors: Arun Kumar Jaiswal, Di Wang, Ji Soo Lim, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant spectroscopy study on 3d/5d oxide heterostructures, touching on electronic structure engineering.

Tags: #heterostructure #oxide #spectroscopy

Abstract: Interfacial charge transfer (ICT) provides a powerful route to engineer electronic phases in correlated oxide heterostructures, yet predictive design principles remain elusive. Here, we systematically investigate superlattices composed of the 5d spin orbit coupled semimetal SrIrO3 and a series of correlated 3d perovskites (LaMnO3, LaFeO3, and LaCoO3), thereby establishing a quantitative framework for ICT across 3d/5d interfaces. Combining Ir L2,3 edge X ray absorption spectroscopy with spatially resolved electron energy loss spectroscopy, we estimate the electron depletion in the SrIrO3 layers and the corresponding electron accumulation in the 3d layers. The magnitude of ICT follows the trend expected from electronegativity mismatch, supporting electronegativity driven band alignment as the dominant contribution in this series. Beyond interfacial doping, we find that strong 3d,5d hybridization induces a low spin to high spin conversion in the cobaltate layers, hinting to interface controlled spin state engineering without chemical substitution. These results establish electronegativity mismatch as a predictive design parameter for correlated oxide interfaces and provide a materials platform for tailoring band filling, orbital hierarchy, and spin configurations in quantum oxide heterostructures, paving the way towards advanced oxide electronics and next-generation information technologies.

item.title: [8] Supermoir\'e reconstruction and domain-resolved valley topology in helical multilayer graphene (2D Mater.)
item.description:
Last authors: Jeil Jung, Hongki Min

Authors: Kyungjin Shin, Nicolas Leconte, Jeil Jung, Hongki Min

Published as: 2D Mater. DOI

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Detailed study on moire systems and topology, relevant to user's broader interest in topological materials.

Tags: #graphene #moire #topological

Abstract: Extending moir\'{e} graphene beyond twisted bilayers, helical trilayer graphene has emerged as a supermoir\'{e} platform hosting topological bands and correlated electronic states. Here we establish a domain-resolved framework for helical multilayer graphene that links supermoir\'{e} relaxation to low-energy electronic structure and valley topology. Real-space lattice calculations show that relaxation reconstructs the system into locally periodic single-moir\'{e} domains, enabling a local continuum description. Within each domain, downfolding the first-shell model yields effective Hamiltonians near the Dirac points that reveal how the low-energy spectrum decomposes into folded Dirac sectors. The resulting valley Chern topology is domain-dependent and includes gate-tunable responses, as independently corroborated by real-space lattice calculations. Our results identify folded Dirac sectors as the organizing principle of thicker helical graphene stacks, with local stacking families determining the band character and valley topology.

item.title: [7] Designing Strong and Broadband Nonreciprocal Thermal Radiation in Magnetic Topological Materials (Nano Lett. (2026))
item.description:
Last authors: Linxiao Zhu, Binghai Yan

Authors: Yiyang Jiang, Yufei Zhao, Linxiao Zhu, Binghai Yan

Published as: Nano Lett. (2026) DOI

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant to magnetic topological materials and Weyl semimetals, though focused on thermal transport.

Tags: #topologicalmaterials #Weyl #anomalousHall

Abstract: Breaking reciprocity in thermal radiation opens opportunities for energy harvesting, sensing, and thermal management. Traditional nonreciprocal radiative semiconductor devices need external magnetic field. In this work, we predict a series of magnetic topological materials for magnetic-field-free nonreciprocal thermal radiation in the infrared regime, by combining first-principles calculations with Maxwell electrodynamics. We find strong and broadband nonreciprocity in magnetic Weyl semimetals (e.g., Co$_3$Sn$_2$S$_2$), outperforming the conventional semiconductor such as InAs. Furthermore, we propose universal material design recipes: strong nonreciprocity requires a large anomalous Hall response relative to the optical loss, whereas the broadband response favors large optical loss and small dielectric dispersion. Our work establishes a predictive materials-discovery framework and quantitative design rules for next-generation magnet-free nonreciprocal thermal devices.

item.title: [7] Steering and Local Tunneling Signatures of Majorana Corner Modes in Altermagnetic Josephson Junctions
item.description:
Last authors: Yu-Xuan Li, Tao Zhou

Score 7/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Altermagnetism and Majorana corner modes are relevant to the topological material interests.; tier capped to C: formal/generic theory watch

Tags: #altermagnetism #Majorana #topological

Abstract: Dynamical manipulation of Majorana zero modes and their reliable distinction from topologically trivial states remain paramount challenges in topological quantum computation. Here, we propose a phase-biased altermagnetic Josephson junction as a versatile platform for generating and controlling Majorana corner configurations. Our platform utilizes the macroscopic superconducting phase difference and the N\'eel-vector orientation as independent control knobs to reshape the boundary mass. This allows the spatial configuration of Majorana corner modes (MCMs) to be selected at different corners of a fixed device geometry. This spatial reconfiguration yields a control-correlated conductance response. Across these configurations, the quantized zero-bias peak appears at the contacted corner in the ideal tunneling model when an MCM is present and is suppressed when it is absent. This correlation connects phase and magnetic control of corner configurations with local tunneling readout.

item.title: [8] Sound attenuation and velocity shift in antiferromagnetic spin-1/2 chains
item.description:
Last authors: Emeric Caprani, Roberta Citro

Authors: Edmond Orignac, Emeric Caprani, Roberta Citro

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relates to 1D Luttinger liquid behavior and spin chain physics.

Tags: #Luttinger #1D #magnetism

Abstract: We investigate ultrasound attenuation and sound velocity shift in antiferromagnetic spin-1/2 XXZ chains in magnetic field. We relate the sound velocity shift to derivatives of the free energy with respect to exchange interactions, permitting its calculation with integrability techniques at any temperature. Using bosonization, we predict the sound velocity shift exhibits a quadratic temperature correction at low temperatures in the Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid phase. Close to the fully polarized phase, a universal behavior associated with z=2 quantum criticality is found. In the Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid phase, ultrasound attenuation obeys a scaling law as a function of wavelength and temperature. An enhancement of attenuation is obtained near the fully polarized phase.

item.title: [7] Interface-Controlled Spin-Orbit Torques in Rare-Earth Synthetic Ferrimagnets Probed by Sagnac Magneto-Optics and Harmonic Hall Measurements
item.description:
Last authors: Andrew D. Kent, J. -Carlos Rojas-S\'anchez

Authors: Akilan K, Koral Aykin, Jose-Luis Ampuero, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of spin-orbit torque and interfaces, relevant to magnetic topological materials research.

Tags: #spin-orbittorque #magnetism #experiment

Abstract: Spin-orbit torque (SOT) provides an efficient route for manipulating magnetization in spintronic devices, and its accurate quantification is essential. Here, we investigate Co/Gd-based synthetic ferrimagnets using complementary magnetotransport and magneto-optical techniques. We use a Sagnac magneto-optical interferometry method to directly quantify current-induced magnetization tilting and extract the damping-like SOT effective field. The Sagnac measurements show good agreement with harmonic Hall analysis across different Co/Gd and Gd/Pt/Co heterostructures, providing a quantitative determination of the damping-like SOT effective field that does not rely on electrical transport signatures. By varying the Gd thickness and multilayer stacking order, we demonstrate that the damping-like torque is strongly influenced by spin transport and angular momentum conversion at rare-earth and heavy-metal interfaces. The observation of a finite torque in Gd/Pt/Co/Pt structures, where conventional Pt spin Hall contributions are expected to compensate, highlights the active role of the Gd layer in SOT generation. Furthermore, interface engineering enables perpendicular magnetic anisotropy in Gd/Pt/Co/Al heterostructures with a 2-nm-thick Co layer, allowing current-induced SOT switching at current densities of 8-10 MA/cm$^2$. These results establish rare-earth-based synthetic ferrimagnets as a versatile platform for engineering spin-orbit phenomena and optimizing low-power spintronic devices.

item.title: [8] Artificial spin ice on the CaVO lattice: a tricritical bridge from square to kagome
item.description:
Last authors: S. Nilsson, V. Scagnoli, P. M. Derlet, L. J. Heyderman

Authors: F. Museur, G. M. Macauley, S. Nilsson, V. Scagnoli, P. M. Derlet, L. J. Heyderman

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant kagome-related geometry and magnetic frustration in a tunable model system.

Tags: #kagome #magnetism #artificial-spin-ice

Abstract: Artificial spin ices (ASIs) are arrays of interacting nanomagnets in which phase transitions can be imaged and controlled. Studies of the thermodynamic have focused mainly on the square and kagome lattices, and on their variants. Here we study artificial spin ice on the CaVO lattice, formed of squares and octagons. At fixed lattice constant, the ratio $r$ of the square and octagon link lengths tunes the interactions strongly while changing the geometry only slightly. Magnetic force microscopy and Monte Carlo simulations show a continuous bridge from square-ice-like to kagome-like behavior. At small $r$ the system has a single ordering transition, whereas at large $r$ it passes from a correlated paramagnet to charge order and then long-range order. The two regimes meet in a multicritical region, accurately modeled by a Blume-Capel model of the octagon toroidal moments. From this picture, we design a comparative magnetometry protocol that unambiguously separates interaction effects from single-nanomagnet effects in thermally active samples. Finally, the charge-ordered region maps onto a tunable dimer model, with a Coulomb phase and pinch points along the line between two ordered dimer phases. The CaVO ASI thus provides access to a rich phase diagram only through geometric tuning, without requiring extreme experimental conditions.

Tags: #Weyl #topological #cold-atoms

Abstract: We propose an interaction-driven route to Weyl superfluidity from topologically trivial noninteracting bands in a three-dimensional optical Raman lattice. The scheme builds on a pairing mechanism arising from the interplay between a large Zeeman splitting and an attractive Hubbard interaction. The large Zeeman splitting renders the noninteracting bands topologically trivial and suppresses spin-flip hopping. item.title: [9] Imaging spin entanglement with a scanning tunneling microscope
item.description:
Last authors: J. C. G. Henriques, B. Vi\~na-Baus\'a, I. Brihuega, J. Fern\'andez-Rossier

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Connects STS to entanglement and quantum spin chains; directly relevant to user STS/electronic structure interest.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #STS #quantum-entanglement #spectroscopy

Abstract: Artificial spin arrays assembled on surfaces enable atomic-scale studies of quantum correlations. Here we establish a hierarchy of connections between spin inelastic electron tunneling spectroscopy (IETS) and entanglement in spin-$1/2$ systems. We first show that the number of spectroscopically active transitions in a spin-$1/2$ dimer serves as an entanglement witness. Using the leading-order tunneling conductance for the tip placed on spin $i$, $dI(i)/dV$, we then relate spectral moments $\mathcal{M}^{(n)}(i)=\int V^n(d^2I(i)/dV^2)\,dV$ to quantum correlations. The zeroth moment probes the one-tangle in systems with a gapped, nondegenerate ground state. For rotationally invariant Heisenberg systems, the first moment yields thermal spin correlators $\langle\boldsymbol S(i)\cdot\boldsymbol S(j)\rangle$, enabling reconstruction of nearest-neighbor concurrence and spatial imaging of entanglement in spin chains. It also provides access to the internal energy and magnetic specific heat, both usable as entanglement witnesses. Applying this approach to experimental IETS data from nanographene spin chains, we find good agreement with theory. We further discuss how the second moment probes longer-range correlations and the inverse moment relates to local spin susceptibility. For spin-$1/2$ trimers, we connect inter-multiplet inelastic spectral weight to genuine tripartite entanglement quantified by the concurrence fill. Finally, we reconcile the local character of IETS with its sensitivity to nonlocal entanglement through an analogy with digital quantum circuits, where Hamiltonian evolution implements multiqubit operations. These results establish IETS as a tool for quantifying and imaging entanglement in engineered on-surface spin systems.

item.title: [8] Tuning correlated states in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene with magnetic encapsulation
item.description:
Last authors: Yitao Sun, Jose L. Lado

Authors: Cuiju Yu, Yitao Sun, Jose L. Lado

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study on correlated states and superconductivity in graphene-based moire-like systems.

Tags: #material #unconventionalsuperconductivity #correlated

Abstract: Rhombohedral graphene multilayers provide a flexible platform for correlated physics associated with their flat-band electronic structure. While a variety of correlated states appear in these systems as a function of bias and electrostatic doping, promoting specific correlated flavor symmetry breaking states remains a challenge. Here we show that magnetic encapsulation by CrGeTe3 achieves this in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene, by using switchable exchange couplings induced by ferromagnetic substrates. We show that correlations in rhombohedral multilayers at charge neutrality strongly renormalize the exchange proximity splitting,giving rise to collective spin modes whose character is switched by the parallel or antiparallel alignment of the encapsulation. We further show that upon doping of the flat bands, spin triplet f-wave superconducting solutions emerge, whose layer and spin selectivity is controlled by the magnetic encapsulation, hosting in-gap excitations at the edges. Our results establish magnetic alignment as a means to control spin symmetry breaking and unconventional superconductivity in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene.

item.title: [8] Hidden Coherence and Controlled Quasihole Motion in a Fermionic Laughlin State on a Superconducting Quantum Processor
item.description:
Last authors: Jian Cui, Heng Fan

Authors: Kui Zhao, Hao Wu, Lei-Yi-Nan Liu, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of fractional quantum Hall physics on a quantum platform; relevant to correlated systems.

Tags: #quantum-hall #strongly-correlated #quantum-simulation

Abstract: Fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states support fractionalized excitations and geometric phases, yet experimentally resolving the many-body coherence encoded in their wave functions remains challenging. Here, we prepare a three-electron $\nu=1/3$ Laughlin state on the Haldane sphere using seven superconducting qubits and reconstruct its many-body density matrix. Through Read's composite-boson construction, we reveal vortex-dressed coherence that remains appreciable over a larger separation range than electron coherence. The extended profile is suppressed in a Fock-diagonal reference constructed from the measured populations, demonstrating its dependence on off-diagonal many-body coherence. We further prepare a one-flux-added quasihole and characterize its fractional charge response against finite-size benchmarks. Controlled quasihole motion yields an effective geometric-phase signature from the reconstructed dominant-eigenstate trajectory. These complementary measurements provide microscopic access to the coherent structure and quasihole response of a finite fermionic Laughlin state, demonstrating an experimental route to probing strongly correlated FQH wave functions on programmable quantum processors.
